questions.title: How exactly is the fastText classifier trained for selecting math web pages in the DeepSeekMath data pipeline?
questions.question_body: The paper says they randomly select 500,000 data points from OpenWebMath as positive examples and another 500,000 web pages from Common Crawl as negative examples, then train a fastText model with vector dimension 256, learning rate 0.1, n‑gram length up to 3, minimum word occurrence 3, and three epochs. I am confused about why these specific numbers were chosen, how sensitive the classifier is to these hyper‑parameters, and whether any validation set was used to tune them before recalling more pages.

questions.title: What techniques constitute “URL‑based deduplication and near‑deduplication” applied to Common Crawl?
questions.question_body: The authors report reducing the original Common Crawl from billions of pages down to 40 B HTML pages using URL‑based deduplication and near‑deduplication, but they do not describe the exact method. Does this involve hashing URLs alone, comparing content fingerprints such as simhash/minhash, or using HTML structure similarity thresholds? Additionally, what percentage of pages were removed at each stage?

questions.title: How does the 10‑gram exact‑match filter remove benchmark contamination?
questions.question_body: To avoid contaminating their training set with test data from GSM8K, MATH, CMATH and AGIEval, the paper states that any text segment containing a 10‑gram string matching exactly a substring from those benchmarks is removed; shorter texts use exact matching for n‑grams ≥ 3. I would like clarification on how these n‑grams are extracted (sliding window over tokenized text?), whether overlapping matches are merged, and roughly how many tokens or webpages were discarded because of this filter.

questions.title: Why do arXiv papers fail to improve mathematical reasoning performance according to DeepSeekMath experiments?
questions.question_body: The authors train models on two arXiv‑centric corpora (MathPile ≈ 8.9 B tokens with > 85% arXiv papers and ArXiv‑RedPajama ≈ 28 B tokens) and observe no notable gains—or even deterioration—on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU‑STEM and miniF2F benchmarks. Could this be due to noisy LaTeX markup, lack of problem‑solving style text, tokenization issues specific to scientific papers, or simply domain mismatch? What evidence do the authors provide supporting any particular hypothesis?

questions.title: What is the intuition behind code pre‑training improving pure mathematical reasoning?
questions.question_body: The paper reports that pre‑training on code tokens first (400 B code tokens → then math tokens) yields better step‑by‑step reasoning on GSM8K/MATH than starting directly from general text pre‑training. I am trying to understand how exposure to programming constructs translates into better algebraic or combinatorial reasoning when no tool use is involved. Do the authors attribute this effect to learning algorithmic patterns, variable handling, or something else?

questions.title: How does Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) replace the critic model used in standard PPO?
questions.question_body: "GRPO foregoes the critic model" by estimating a baseline from group scores instead of learning a value function. For each question q it samples a group of G outputs {o₁,…,o_G} from the old policy π_old then computes advantages \hat{A}_{i,t} based on relative rewards within that group. I would like a step‑by‑step description of how \hat{A}_{i,t} is calculated—in particular whether it uses simple mean subtraction or a more sophisticated estimator—and how changing G influences variance reduction compared with using an explicit learned value network.

questions.title: Why does GRPO add a KL divergence term directly to its loss instead of incorporating KL penalty into rewards like PPO?
questions.question_body: In PPO the per‑token reward includes −β·log[π_θ/π_ref] (Eq. 2), whereas GRPO adds −β·D_KL[π_θ || π_ref] directly into its objective (Eq. 4). What are the practical benefits of moving KL regularization out of the reward computation—for example stability or easier advantage estimation—and how does their unbiased KL estimator \(π_ref/π_θ − log(π_ref/π_θ) − 1\) guarantee positivity?

questions.title: What distinguishes outcome supervision from process supervision in GRPO’s advantage computation?
questions.question_body: "Outcome supervision" assigns \hat{A}_{i,t}=\widetilde{r}_i (the normalized final reward) identically to every token in output o_i, while "process supervision" provides stepwise rewards r_i^{index(j)} at each reasoning step j and defines \hat{A}_{i,t}=∑_{index(j)>=t}\widetilde{r}_i^{index(j)}. Could someone explain how step boundaries are detected in practice (e.g., special markers), how normalization across all steps works mathematically, and what empirical impact each method has on learning efficiency?

questions.title: How is iterative reinforcement learning performed with GRPO’s reward model update via replay?
questions.question_body: "Iterative RL" continuously retrains the reward model using newly sampled policy outputs along with a replay buffer containing ~10% historical data. I would appreciate details such as (1) how many new samples are collected per iteration before updating r_φ?, (2) what optimizer settings and learning rates are used for r_φ?, (3) whether older samples are weighted differently than fresh ones during replay.

questions.title: "Self‑consistency over 64 samples" – what procedure produces this improvement?
questions.(The abstract mentions that self‑consist: I would also like clarification on whether temperature / nucleus sampling settings differ when generating those multiple samples.

questions.title: How were informal-to-formal theorem proving tasks evaluated on miniF2F using DeepSeekMath-Base?
questions.question_body: The paper states that DeepSeekMath-Base generates proof sketches which are fed into Sledgehammer (Isabelle’s automated prover). I would like specifics on (1) prompt format used for generating sketch statements/joint lemmas versus full formal proofs; (2) number of few-shot examples supplied; (3) success criterion—does passing Sledgehammer’s automatic proof count as correct even if human verification isn’t performed?

questions.title: Why does reinforcement learning improve Maj@K accuracy but not Pass@K according to DeepSeekMath analysis?
questions.question_body: Figure 9 shows that after RL training Maj@K rises while Pass@K stays roughly unchanged across K values for GSM8K/MATH. Does this indicate that RL mainly reshapes probability mass toward already high-scoring candidates rather than increasing overall competence? How should this observation guide future RL design for reasoning tasks?

questions.title: In the unified paradigm equation (13), what form does Gradient Coefficient GC_𝓐 take for DPO compared with PPO/GRPO?
questions.question_body: The authors express every method’s gradient as E[(q,o)] GC_𝓐(q,o,t,… )∇θlogπθ(o_t|…). For DPO they mention pairwise preference loss—but I cannot locate an explicit expression for GC_DPO(q,o,…). Could someone derive GC_DPO mathematically and contrast it with GC_PPO which involves clipped probability ratios times advantage?

questions.title: Do diminishing returns appear when scaling pre‑training data beyond roughly 120 B tokens?
questions.question_body: Figure 2 shows performance curves for top 40B/80B/120B/160B token subsets; after four iterations they stop at ∼120 B because ∼98% coverage was already achieved earlier. Can we quantify how much accuracy improvement extra tokens beyond 120 B bring on GSM8K/MATH benchmarks? Is there evidence of flattening curves indicating saturation?

questions.title: How were multilingual portions (English & Chinese) handled during tokenization and vocabulary construction for DeepSeekMath?
questions.question_body: The corpus contains both English and Chinese web pages thoroughly mixed during pre‑training. Did they use a shared byte‑pair encoding vocabulary trained jointly on both languages? Were there any language‐specific preprocessing steps such as Unicode normalization or script detection before tokenization?
